reviews.title: Never again
reviews.text:
Disappointing Service – Not Worth the Subscription Fee

Unfortunately, F1 TV is no longer worth the money. The casting functionality is extremely unreliable, frequently disconnecting and making it unnecessarily difficult to watch races on a larger screen.

I have been a subscriber for several years, but the ongoing technical issues are becoming increasingly frustrating. Rather than enhancing the Formula 1 viewing experience, the app is actually discouraging me from watching the sport.

For a premium subscription service associated with a global brand like Formula 1, I expect a much higher standard of quality, reliability and performance.

It is disappointing that such a fundamental feature as casting does not work properly. This is simply not the level of service that Formula 1 fans should have to accept.

F1 TV needs significant improvement. In its current state, it is difficult to justify the subscription cost. This is simply not worthy of the F1 brand.

reviews.title: Unreliable streams, spoiled results and a deeply frustrating
reviews.text:
Starting a stream on F1 TV is often a struggle, especially during a live Grand Prix. I regularly have to try several times before I can actually get in.

Once the stream finally starts, it frequently cuts out. Restarting it can send me straight to the live action instead of resuming where I left off. Even worse, the app sometimes displays the result while I am only halfway through the race, precisely because its interruptions and login problems have put me behind. Having the result spoiled by the very service I am using to watch the race is incredibly frustrating.

I have an excellent 1 Gbps internet connection, yet these problems keep happening.

The transition from the pre-race show to the race itself is equally annoying. When the pre-race programme ends, I have to manually open a separate race stream and log in again. That often fails too, possibly because of high demand. Why is there no seamless transition between the two?

Unfortunately, Viaplay is no real alternative here in the Netherlands either, because I find its presenters absolutely awful.

For a paid service dedicated to Formula 1, reliably starting a race, keeping it playing and remembering my position should be basic requirements. Instead, watching a Grand Prix becomes a battle with the app.

Overall, a terrible experience that takes much of the enjoyment out of watching F1.

reviews.title: Airplay Doesn’t Work Half the Time
reviews.text:
The app itself works well, and quick access to all cameras during a race is decently implemented, but trying to screencast the race through airplay is genuinely one of the most frustrating experiences I’ve dealt with. 
Once you start screencasting, everything starts to buffer, takes forever to load, and once it loads there’s a 50% chance it only plays for 15 seconds and buffers again, OR it restarts the entire broadcast again and proceeds to buffer. Not to mention while screencasting if you choose to view the race live or from the beginning, it ignores your choice and just goes to the live feed anyway.
It’s quite the joke that Apple and F1 are official partners and they can’t even get the software to work together properly.

reviews.title: Abysmal is too much flattery
reviews.text:
Writing a review for the android TV here since I for sure will not do that using my remote om the television.

- There is no time table in the app for upcoming live broadcasts. Every streaming/television implementation has this since the Ming dynasty. Step out of feudal middle ages please.

- Somehow the UX designers though they could "improve" on standard controls. It now takes two (obscure) presses on my remote to pause the stream instead of one, or at least obvious on screen pointers to tell me my options. 

- Satans Autoplay. Autoplay makes one of Dantes lower levels feel like a weekend out in a cabana in Mexico with free complimentary beverages and snacks. Not only can you not switch off Autoplay but it also always defaults to the last upload, even if you have already watched it. It will hower not move over to the next Livestream, like going from the pre-race show to the race. This makes you frantically zap your way through many screens to find the correct next stream just in time to have to rewind back to view the cars leave the starting line. By the time you are settled your beverages have gone lukewarm.

reviews.title: What a Blown Opportunity
reviews.text: I have been a stateside Formula One fan for over a decade. The F1 TV service has been the crown jewel of my sports watching experience. There was access to an archive of F1 races, multiple commentary options, and everything simplified into a price plan that could be paid yearly with no blackouts or restrictions whatsoever. This year, F1 decided to sell out and package everything into Apple TV. Not only are there now commercials, sponsored screen overlays, an unavoidable monthly charge that is subject to price hikes, making the entire flow of what made F1 so good now crushed. I do not understand what the point of this was. F1 knew they were in a great position to attract American motorsport fans. This legitimately makes me consider never paying for the service again and switching over to a different motorsport series.

reviews.title: CORPORATE GREED
reviews.text: They have officially killed the only way for Americans to watch the sport. Going to Apple is the death of the growth this sport was seeing in America. For the last 5 years I have watched every race, practice, sprint and qualifying session. Then when it was out of season I could watch any race I wanted to and learn about the history of the sport. In depth analysis from the F1TV crew during the week leading up and during the weekend helped me gain interest in the sport and it is a shame you are choosing corporate partnership over consumer protection. The $17 a month I paid this last year, a steap price increase, just for the ability to watch a multiview, was for not as now I cannot access any live races given they all moved to the worst platform and company ever APPLE! This is just a slap in the face to your consumer base and I will just simply not be watching anymore given I don’t have access. Congrats on taking away the one good thing about F1 coverage, it wasn’t predatory, multiple tiers for which you could choose, and it had every single category of racing live. That was too good for us consumers the corporations thought, “why are we making these people’s lives easier, they should pay more for that!”. Now you isolated yourself to Apple TV where .05% of the US population actually uses it. Congrats.
